root_cause.text: The `cgroup_storage_get_next_key()` function incorrectly relied on `list_next_entry()` returning NULL to detect the end of a linked list, but `list_next_entry()` never returns NULL—it wraps to the list head via `container_of()`, causing the NULL check to be dead code and allowing out-of-bounds memory reads from bogus pointers that alias internal map fields.
root_cause.evidence: The patch replaces the ineffective NULL check (`if (!storage)`) with `list_entry_is_head(storage, &map->list, list_map)`, which properly detects when iteration has wrapped back to the list head. The CVE description explicitly states that "list_next_entry() never returns NULL -- when the current element is the last entry it wraps to the list head via container_of()" and that the function was "reading storage->key from a bogus pointer that aliases internal map fields and copying the result to userspace" instead of correctly returning -ENOENT.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix incorrect null check after list_next_entry() by using list_entry_is_head() to properly detect end-of-list condition.
intent_record.what: Replaced a null pointer check `if (!storage)` with a list boundary check `if (list_entry_is_head(storage, &map->list, list_map))` after calling `list_next_entry()`.
intent_record.how: The original code attempted to check if `storage` was null, but `list_next_entry()` never returns null—it returns a pointer to the next list node or wraps around to the list head. The new code correctly detects when iteration has wrapped to the list head (end of iteration) using the kernel's `list_entry_is_head()` macro, preventing infinite loops or incorrect behavior when reaching the end of the cgroup storage list.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable function `cgroup_storage_get_next_key()` is present in lines 147-177. The bug exists at line 161: `storage = list_next_entry(storage, list);` followed by line 162: `if (!storage)`. The `list_next_entry()` macro never returns NULL—it uses `container_of()` to wrap around to the list head when reaching the end. Therefore, the NULL check on line 162 is dead code and will never be true. When the end of the list is reached, `storage` will point to the list head structure itself (aliasing internal map fields), allowing the function to proceed to lines 165-167 where it reads from this bogus pointer: `next->attach_type = storage->key.attach_type; next->cgroup_inode_id = storage->key.cgroup_inode_id;`. This causes out-of-bounds memory reads. The fix is not present—the code should use `list_is_last()` or similar to properly detect the end of the list before calling `list_next_entry()`.
